files.description: Authoritative developer onboarding for DAQIRI: build commands, the benchmarks-as-tests model, the Engine/BurstParams architecture, the DPDK build dependency, the CMake socket->rdma rule, current public-API limitations, and the doc-sync drift hotspots. Read this first.
Project contribution rules: mandatory local PR checks, clang-format, DCO sign-off, '#<Issue Number> - <Title>' commit format, prefer-CMake-over-ifdef policy, narrow PRs, and the fork-and-PR workflow.

Required local pre-PR entry point. It creates an isolated virtual environment, runs portable tests and fast documentation validation, and optionally regenerates packet diagrams or builds the Docker base stage.
Local container release procedure: build/push the host-architecture image, then publish and inspect the canonical amd64+arm64 manifest after both architecture tags exist.
The sole retained GitHub Actions workflow. It may build, validate, and deploy documentation; general tests, builds, and container publication must remain local.
Source-of-truth mapping from source-file changes to the docs that must be updated in the same PR. Use this to decide whether a code-change PR also needs doc updates.
Public aggregate C++ API header for the free-function surface operating on opaque BurstParams batches. Application code should include and use this surface rather than engine types.
Public types: BurstParams, Status, NetworkConfig, MemoryKind, Direction, SocketProtocol, and engine-selection types. Field changes or new enum values trigger API documentation review.

daqiri::Engine virtual interface and EngineFactory singleton. Every engine lives behind this vtable. Adding a new engine means adding a src/engines/<name>/ subclass, NOT branching on engine type at call sites.

Build system for the common library and per-engine libraries. Owns DAQIRI_ENGINE parsing, the ibverbs-to-rdma internal mapping, the always-built socket engine, DAQIRI_ENGINE_<NAME>=1 definitions, and CUDA architecture defaults.
C++ API guide and BurstParams ownership contract. Update it with changes to public headers, Engine behavior exposed through the flat API, or call patterns.

Top-level project overview: Quick Start build commands, Engines table, Documentation table, Features list, and limitations. Update in sync with engines, build configuration, public headers, and documentation renames.
